name: Graphide
long_description:
Coding agents now write more code than teams can check, so verification decides how much software ships. Graphide builds that verification, starting with CI.

Graphide CI runs a team's GitHub Actions 10–20× faster than GitHub's hosted runners, and cheaper. We control both the hardware and the optimizations on top of it, which lets us do what a faster runner or a smarter config can't do alone: a graph of the codebase limits each change to the tests it can reach, our own libraries and patches make the tests themselves run faster, and always-on agents tune machines, caches and test splits together, around the clock. A failing test always fails the job. One customer cut CI time 92% against its existing setup.

Graphide review checks every pull request: an agent runs the old and new code in a live environment to prove what breaks, and a visualizer shows the approver what changed. The first 150 reviews are free.

Agents write the code. Graphide verifies it.

founders.title: Founder/CEO
founders.founder_bio: CEO and co-founder of Graphide. Ran a software automation business in high school, then studied EECS and Business at UC Berkeley through the M.E.T. program. While at Illumio as an intern, built Matrix, the policy simulation platform Illumio uses today, orchestrating networks of 300+ VMs and simulating attacks across them. Left Berkeley to start Graphide.

founders.title: Founder/CTO
founders.founder_bio: Founder at Graphide. Founded and led the University of Cincinnati Linux and FOSS club, growing it to over 100 students. Previously ran tech operations for a political campaign, building custom voter outreach systems. Studying Computer Engineering and Mathematics at UC.
